clue.text: A mere puppet of Stravinsky

parts.note: points to the title character of a Stravinsky ballet, a straw-stuffed fairground puppet who comes to life

explanation.walkthrough: A general-knowledge cryptic definition: 'A mere puppet' teases the ballet's hero, a puppet who has feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: Stravinsky's 1911 ballet takes its title from a Russian fairground puppet, so the name is that puppet's.

clue.text: "Like a rich jewel in an -'s ear" (Romeo and Juliet)

definitions.text: "Like a rich jewel in an -'s ear" (Romeo and Juliet)

parts.words: "Like a rich jewel in an -'s ear" (Romeo and Juliet)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Romeo's first sight of Juliet, the gap being an old word for an African

explanation.walkthrough: A quotation clue: supply the missing word from Act 1 Scene 5 of the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo says Juliet hangs on night's cheek like a jewel in an African's ear, using Shakespeare's word for an Ethiopian.

clue.text: Became more amenable concerning fast journalist

parts.note: re is a crossword word for concerning or about
Lent is the Christian season of fasting
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Someone softens their stance about a journalist who works quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like an adjective for the journalist, but it is the noun: a period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to soften and give way, so someone who relented grew more yielding.

clue.text: The way down to it is easy, Virgil tells us

definitions.text: The way down to it is easy, Virgil tells us

parts.words: The way down to it is easy, Virgil tells us
parts.note: alludes to the Aeneid's line facilis descensus Averno, the descent to Avernus, the realm of the dead, being easy

explanation.walkthrough: Aeneid Book 6: 'facilis descensus Averno', the easy descent; coming back up is the hard part.
explanation.definitionFit: Avernus in the Aeneid stands for Hades, the realm of the dead beneath the earth.

clue.text: Horror is his Domain and Creed

definitions.text: Horror is his Domain and Creed

parts.words: Horror is his Domain and Creed
parts.note: reads as a horror writer's credo, but Domain and Creed are titles of novels by the British horror novelist James ...

explanation.walkthrough: The capitals give it away: Domain and Creed are book titles, not just a way of saying horror is his speciality.
explanation.definitionFit: James Herbert, British horror novelist, wrote the books Domain (1984) and Creed (1990).

clue.text: Assert the beginnings of a very exceptional renaissance

indicators.note: the opening letters of each of the following four words are taken

explanation.surface: Someone claims we are seeing a truly remarkable revival.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state firmly, a formal synonym for declare.

clue.text: His English was basic, but his criticism new

definitions.text: His English was basic, but his criticism new

parts.words: His English was basic, but his criticism new
parts.note: sounds like a jibe, but describes I. A. ..., who promoted Basic English and helped found the New Criticism

explanation.walkthrough: 'basic' and 'new' are not insults or praise: they name Basic English and the New Criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: I. A. Richards worked with C. K. Ogden on Basic English and his Practical Criticism shaped the New Critics.

clue.text: Wrecked shop annexe reveals philosopher

indicators.note: a wrecked building is smashed up, so the letters of the two following words are broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A ruined shop extension turns up a thinker hiding inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrecked' rearranges SHOPANNEXE into the name of the pre-Socratic Greek thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenophanes of Colophon was a Greek pre-Socratic thinker and poet.

clue.text: Scene of decline of Corvo and von Aschenbach

definitions.text: Scene of decline of Corvo and von Aschenbach

parts.words: Scene of decline of Corvo and von Aschenbach
parts.note: Baron Corvo (Frederick Rolfe) sank into poverty and died in an Italian lagoon city, where Mann's Aschenbach dies too

explanation.walkthrough: Gustav von Aschenbach is the hero of Thomas Mann's novella; Corvo was the pen-name of Frederick Rolfe.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolfe spent his last destitute years in that Italian city, and Mann set Death in Venice there.

clue.text: An operatic Tom Jones not one of his better gambits

definitions.text: An operatic Tom Jones not one of his better gambits

parts.words: An operatic Tom Jones not one of his better gambits
parts.note: points to the French composer and chess master who wrote an opera of Tom Jones and gave his name to a chess opening

explanation.walkthrough: 'gambits' looks like a joke about his career moves, but Philidor also gave his name to a chess defence and gambit.
explanation.definitionFit: François-André Danican Philidor composed the opéra comique Tom Jones (1765) and was the leading chess player of his age.

clue.text: Shakespearean anti-Hero

parts.note: not a flawed protagonist but a character working against Hero, the slandered bride in Much Ado About Nothing

explanation.walkthrough: 'anti-Hero' looks like the literary term, but the capital H names the heroine he plots against.
explanation.definitionFit: Borachio, Don John's follower in Much Ado About Nothing, stages the deception that disgraces Hero.

clue.text: "… In a corner, some untidy ——' / Where the dogs go on with their doggy life" (W. H. Auden)

definitions.text: "… In a corner, some untidy ——' / Where the dogs go on with their doggy life" (W. H. Auden)

parts.words: "… In a corner, some untidy ——' / Where the dogs go on with their doggy life" (W. H. Auden)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Auden's poem Musée des Beaux Arts, the gap being a small place

explanation.walkthrough: A quotation clue: supply the missing word from Auden's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: In Musée des Beaux Arts the martyrdom happens anyhow, in an untidy place where dogs carry on.

clue.text: Fuller version of uncivilized wealth

parts.note: savage means wild or uncivilized
gold stands for riches or wealth

explanation.surface: A fuller account of primitive riches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fuller' looks like 'more complete', but it is the English writer Roy Fuller, whose novel for children Savage Gold (1946) is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Savage Gold is an adventure novel by Roy Fuller, so it is a Fuller book.

clue.text: Balladist setting value on text

indicators.note: in an across clue, setting one piece on another places it after

parts.note: a text is made of words
worth means value

explanation.surface: Someone sets a price on a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth co-wrote the Lyrical Ballads with Coleridge, so he is a writer of ballads.

clue.text: Seth, who offered better than cold comfort

definitions.text: Seth, who offered better than cold comfort

parts.words: Seth, who offered better than cold comfort
parts.note: points to the brooding, sexy farm son Seth in Stella Gibbons's comic novel Cold Comfort Farm

explanation.walkthrough: 'cold comfort' is the novel Cold Comfort Farm (1932); Seth's appeal to the village girls is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Seth Starkadder is the handsome, smouldering son of the family at Cold Comfort Farm.

clue.text: Rev rued devastation of poetic greenery

indicators.note: devastation lays waste, so the letters of the clergyman and his regret are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A vicar regrets the destruction of the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devastation of' rearranges REVRUED. 'Rev' is fodder, not the reverend.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdure is a literary word for lush green vegetation.

clue.text: Elevated by 70s duo for J. D. Salinger?

definitions.text: Elevated by 70s duo for J. D. Salinger?

parts.words: Elevated by 70s duo for J. D. Salinger?
parts.note: rewrites the Salinger title Raise High the ... Carpenters as if Carpenters were the 1970s brother-and-sister pop duo

explanation.walkthrough: The Carpenters were a 1970s pop duo; Salinger's novella is Raise High the Roof Beam, Carpenters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Salinger's title the carpenters are told to raise high the beam holding up the roof.

clue.text: Powerful chap, we hear (with money), encountered in the company of Quilp

definitions.text: encountered in the company of Quilp

indicators.note: the money is held with, inside, the strong man's name

parts.note: Samson is the strongman of the Book of Judges
P stands for pence, money

explanation.surface: A strong man with cash is met alongside a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' marks that the name sounds just like the strongman's: the P is silent. Sampson Brass is Quilp's crooked lawyer in Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Sampson Brass is Quilp's attorney and accomplice in The Old Curiosity Shop.

clue.text: American humorist, and father of the French student chap

parts.note: père is French for father
L for learner, a student driver's plate
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: A comic writer with a French dad and a son at college.
explanation.definitionFit: S. J. Perelman was an American comic writer for The New Yorker and the Marx Brothers.

clue.text: Dramatist reveals extra amount about deception

indicators.note: the extra amount goes around the deception

parts.note: more is an additional quantity
a lie is a deception

explanation.surface: A playwright shows extra amount surrounding a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reveals' is a link word. Fittingly, the playwright's Tartuffe is a comedy built on a hypocrite's deceit.
explanation.definitionFit: Molière was the great French comic playwright of Tartuffe, itself a play about deception.

clue.text: Preliminary preparation for Asimov masterpiece?

parts.note: preliminary preparation is a basis, and the question mark hints at a synonym of Asimov's novel Foundation

explanation.walkthrough: Asimov's Foundation trilogy; the answer is another word for foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: Foundation is Asimov's most famous series, and a foundation is basic preparatory work.

clue.text: Bare bones, part of primer Ibsen wrote 18

indicators.note: part of the run of words primer Ibsen holds the answer within it

explanation.surface: The skeleton of a basic Ibsen reader.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across primeR IBSen. 'wrote 18' points to the Ibsen-flavoured cross-reference and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribs are bones of the chest, here the bare bones of a skeleton.

clue.text: Flowers like Molly and Leopold

explanation.surface: Flowers like those two Irish lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: Molly and Leopold Bloom are the married couple at the heart of Joyce's Ulysses.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowering plants burst into flower, and Molly and Leopold share the surname of Joyce's married couple.

clue.text: Archangel I perceived at the organ in St Mark's

definitions.text: at the organ in St Mark's

parts.note: Gabriel is the archangel of the Annunciation

explanation.surface: Someone sees the archangel at the organ in a Venetian church.
explanation.walkthrough: Giovanni Gabrieli was principal organist at St Mark's, Venice, around 1600.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Gabrieli held the post of organist at St Mark's Basilica in Venice.

clue.text: Looked at part of Northanger Abbey edition

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the words Northanger Abbey edition, spanning two of them

explanation.surface: Someone examines a section of a copy of the Austen novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across abbEY EDition.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyed means watched or looked over.

clue.text: Hardly Disraeli's novel version of "the brainsick shepherd prince"

definitions.text: Hardly Disraeli's novel version of "the brainsick shepherd prince"

parts.words: Hardly Disraeli's novel version of "the brainsick shepherd prince"
parts.note: Disraeli wrote a novel with this title, but the brainsick shepherd prince is Keats's hero, the shepherd loved by the moon goddess

explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' hints at both Disraeli's novel and that his book is no new version of Keats's story.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats's long poem tells of the shepherd prince loved by the moon goddess; Disraeli's last novel has the same title.

clue.text: Holmes investigated one of strawberry blonds

definitions.text: Holmes investigated one of strawberry blonds

parts.words: Holmes investigated one of strawberry blonds
parts.note: strawberry blonds are red-heads, pointing to the Conan Doyle story about an association of red-headed men

explanation.walkthrough: 'strawberry blonds' is a playful stand-in for red-headed.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Red-Headed League Holmes looks into a sham society that only red-haired men may join.

clue.text: "There's a —— in dedicated spirits" (Christopher Fry)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from the English verse dramatist Christopher Fry, the gap being a word for dullness

explanation.walkthrough: A quotation clue: supply the missing word from Christopher Fry.
explanation.definitionFit: Fry's line suggests devoted people can be dull and gloomy company.
